evidence: Swap test: fails for the visual frame (a GP-surgery appointment form or a library room booking could take the pale-green ground, white bordered cards, bold sans headings, outlined day chips, slot-tile grid and single green button unchanged); passes for the copy and content ('20-minute slot you will arrive in; the gate checks the reference and the vehicle', 'Starts DRC-, then five digits', 'Rubble (up to four bags)', 'This booking is not on the gate's list').

Category-guess: fails; the predicted default for a UK council service (government-design-system form: masthead with council name, step list, outlined/filled green buttons, error summary box with red border, bordered summary list with 'Change' links) matches nearly every visual element.
Similar-prompt: fails for visuals; a brief for a council garden-waste-collection or a swimming-pool lane booking would land on the same page.
What belongs to the product: the slot grid with 'Few left'/'Full' tags (the scarcity mechanism made visible), the gate-attendant voice, and the DR- reference on the done page.
No signature beyond that; the masthead identity is only 'Dunmore District Council' in bold body text beside a generic bin glyph.

unfinished: identity is only the council name in body-size bold text with a stock bin icon; nothing in the masthead or ground says recycling centre or Quarry Road
no focal point on the done page: the reference DR-204117 is a 32px bold line inside a generic card, not something that reads as a pass to show at the gate

half-empty columns at 1280/1440: forms and text run to ~610-700px while their containing cards stretch to 1088px, leaving large empty white card areas (done 'Your reference' card, 'Opening days' card, confirm 'Your booking' card)
empty band below the footer on the done page at 1280 (footer stops at ~715px of a 900px viewport, pale ground continues beneath)
the vehicle page is a heading and a stack of identical checkbox rows: sections that are only a heading and a list
headings differ from body mainly by size and weight in the same face; no typographic moment anywhere
the 'At the centre' card stops at half width next to a full-width reference card for no visible reason
evidence: Seen as a resident on a phone the evening before: root/slot-chosen/375-light shows a tidy, legible government-style form with the slot grid as the only thing to look at; vehicle/van/1280-light is a white list of seven checkbox rows; confirm/default/1280-light is a summary card plus four empty inputs; done/default/1280-light is two bordered cards and an outlined button, with an empty pale band under the footer. Everything is clean and orderly, the dark theme is composed, but nothing is finished beyond the default: it reads as a well-built default form, not something the council would be proud of as its recycling centre's face.
